Purposefully driven, innovative, globally impactful
The Faculty of Science and Engineering is a young and dynamic faculty driven by the spirit of discovery. Here we nurture the next generation of science and technology innovators.
From a handful of students on the University’s first day, the faculty now serves 6500 students across all our programs.
Our research and teaching addresses the big issues faced by society in Australia and globally:
artificial intelligence
accelerating climate impacts
translating bioinnovation
addressing nationwide skills shortages in engineering and computing.
The pairing of engineering and science in a single faculty means many of our research discoveries in science see direct technological applications in engineering.
Our research excellence
The Faculty of Science and Engineering includes many research centres and groups, and is home to over half of Macquarie University’s Centres of Research Excellence.
We are active in many industry partnerships, commercial collaborations and joint enterprise initiatives with government, industry and business partners.
Our schools and departments
The faculty consists of:
four schools:
Computing
Engineering
Mathematical and Physical Sciences
Natural Sciences.
two research departments:
Applied BioSciences
Australian Astronomical Optics.
Our passionate staff and engaged coursework and graduate research students are dedicated to the advancement of science and engineering in the 21st century. View our schools and departments.
Graduate research degrees
We supervise and progress graduate research students undertaking their research masters and PhDs across a wide range of specialist discipline areas.
We provide research training pathways for students from Australia and around the globe.
Our foundations and future
The strength of our faculty lies in our people: the students, educators, researchers and partners who turn ideas into impact. As Executive Dean, it gives me great pleasure to introduce the new 2026–2030 Faculty of Science and Engineering Strategy.
Professor Samuel Muller
Faculty Executive Dean
